## Directory

### Coding & Vibe Coding
- [Cursor](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/cursor): AI-first code editor with agent mode, codebase chat and tab completion. Now sold as part of The X Subscription (Oct 13, 2026); existing Cursor plans keep working as legacy plans. The Cursor Agent SDK (announced Oct 20, 2026, GA in v0.3.0 on Oct 23) lets you write your own agents as code, with prompts in Markdown and tools as TypeScript functions, built-in evals and a local playground, then deploy them to Cursor or self-host them in a container; it is the framework behind Cursor's own Bugbot and Security Review. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, an open-weight model with a 1M-token context, was added Oct 26 and is billed as a third-party model. Pricing: Plus from $8/mo (Grok models only); Premium $30/mo adds cloud agents and third-party models at API list price. Free tier: yes.
- [Bolt.new](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/bolt-new): Prompt, run, edit and deploy full-stack web apps right in your browser. Pricing: Pro from $25/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [v0](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/v0): Vercel's AI app builder that turns prompts into React/Next.js apps and UI. Pricing: Plus from $30/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Lovable](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/lovable): Build full-stack web apps by chatting with an AI engineer. New Oct 20, 2026: Lovable can create a Supabase project for an app with no backend (you pick the organization and region, and Supabase bills your own organization), and companies with several Lovable workspaces can group them into one organization with shared SSO and SCIM. Also Oct 20: n8n and LlamaParse connectors, plus ByteDance's Seedream 5 Pro image model and Seedance 2.5 video model for app features (an admin enables ByteDance in Connectors first). Pricing: Pro from $25/mo ($21/mo billed annually); free plan has 5 daily credits. Free tier: yes.
- [Replit](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/replit): Browser IDE with Replit Agent that builds and deploys apps from a prompt. New Oct 22, 2026: Monitoring Agent, an on-call agent for published apps. Turn on monitoring alerts and Auto-fix and it investigates production issues from your app's logs and metrics, attempts and validates a fix and emails you a summary; with the experimental Auto-republish setting it can also publish the fix. Replit hasn't published fix-accuracy numbers. Pricing: Core from $20/mo ($18/mo billed annually). Free tier: yes.
- [GitHub Copilot](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/github-copilot): AI pair programmer and coding agent inside VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub. New at GitHub Universe (Oct 28, 2026): Copilot Fusion is generally available. Pick Fusion instead of a model and Copilot routes each step of a task across one or more models (GitHub says Fusion Max scored within two points of Opus 5.5 Max on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at half the cost; that is GitHub's claim). Also new: a redesigned GitHub Copilot app for issue-to-merge agent work, Copilot projects that run parallel agent sessions across several repos, automations that propose improvements from past runs, and Copilot code review Max, which runs several review agents on different models and merges their findings. GitHub Enterprise customers can now use every Copilot feature without a separate Copilot subscription and pay for the AI credits they use (through GitHub Sales for now). Pricing: Pro from $10/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Devin](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/devin): Cognition's coding agents: Devin Desktop (the editor formerly called Windsurf) plus Devin cloud agents. Fusion mode in Devin Desktop and CLI pairs a frontier lead model with a cheaper sidekick; with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna it scores 68.1 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Pro includes free use of Cognition's own SWE-2 model. Pricing: Free plan; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams from $80/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Zed](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/zed): Fast open-source code editor with AI edit predictions, an agent panel and bring-your-own-key support. Pricing: Pro from $10/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [OpenRouter](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/openrouter): One OpenAI-compatible API for 500+ models from 80+ providers, with fallback routing. Pricing: Pay-as-you-go; 5.5% fee on credit purchases. Free tier: yes.
- [Muse Spark Open (Meta)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/muse-spark-open-meta): Meta's open-weight multimodal MoE model (816B total, 42B active, 1M context) built for coding and agent work. Released Oct 15, 2026. Pricing: Free open weights (Muse Model License); hosted via OpenRouter, Groq, Together and others. Free tier: yes.
- [NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-bolt): NVIDIA's open local model (74B total, 9B active, 256K context) for coding, reasoning, vision and tool use. Fits about 24GB of GPU memory via Ollama, llama.cpp or LM Studio (NVIDIA GPUs; no Apple silicon yet). Released Oct 15, 2026. New Oct 23: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, a small 4B-effective model (built on Gemma 4 E4B) for fast local voice and device assistants with multi-turn tool use, a conversational mode and switchable reasoning. NVIDIA's 4GB Q4_K_M GGUF used about 3.5-4.3GB of VRAM on an RTX 5070 in its tests; in Ollama it's nemotron-3.5-bolt:e4b (7.2-7.9GB download with image input, plus MLX builds for Apple silicon). Pricing: Free open weights (OpenMDW License 1.1). Free tier: yes.
- [OpenCode](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/opencode): Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, desktop app and IDE. Use its free included models, connect 75+ providers (including local models), or sign in with GitHub Copilot or ChatGPT Plus/Pro. Security note: on Oct 17, 2026 OpenCode disclosed a breach of a legacy system behind its hosted Console that may have exposed provider API keys saved in Console workspaces (1.4% of Console users, all notified by email). Keys you add locally in the CLI or desktop app weren't part of it. Since then Anthropic has revoked affected Claude keys, Google has blocked exposed Gemini keys, OpenAI has refunded API credits used in the attack and OpenCode says its own refunds are underway. If you were notified, replace those keys and check usage back to Oct 16. OpenCode 2.0 (announced Oct 12) runs one shared background service for the terminal, web and desktop apps, with a rebuilt API and background subagents. It ships as a separate package (@opencode/cli); the default install still gives you 1.x, and V1 plugins don't work on 2.0. Pricing: Open source (MIT); optional Zen pay-as-you-go models. Free tier: yes.
- [Recursive Flint](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/recursive-flint): Recursive's first model: an open-weight mixture-of-experts coding model (39.8B total, about 2.5B active per token) built for fast agentic coding on your own machine. Recursive says it leads MoE models under 50B parameters on SWE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Verified, and runs at 125+ tokens/sec on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro. Runs via Ollama (flint:40b), llama.cpp, LM Studio, Unsloth, vLLM or SGLang; the INT4 GGUF needs a 48GB Apple Silicon Mac and Unsloth's 3-bit GGUF fits 24GB RAM. Released Oct 21, 2026; Recursive says it may need more step-by-step guidance than big closed models. Pricing: Free open weights (Apache-2.0). Free tier: yes.
- [MiniMax M3.1 Flash](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/minimax-m3-1-flash): MiniMax's open-weight multimodal mixture-of-experts model (about 428B total, 23B active per token, up to 1M tokens of context) for coding, agentic work, computer use and cybersecurity tasks. Takes text, image and video input. MiniMax's own benchmarks put it at 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 61.7 on OSWorld 2.0, close to big closed models on several agent tests. Too big for a home PC: MiniMax recommends serving it with SGLang, vLLM or TokenSpeed, or using it through MiniMax Agent and the MiniMax API. New in October 2026. Pricing: Free open weights (MiniMax Community License: commercial use needs a 'Built with MiniMax M3.1-Flash' credit and a notice to MiniMax; written approval above $20M yearly revenue). Free tier: yes.
- [Nanbeige4.3-33B](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/nanbeige4-3-33b): Open-weight 33B dense model from the Nanbeige team, built for agentic coding and office-style agent tasks (tool use, planning, multi-step work), with a thinking mode you can switch off and up to 512K tokens of context. On Nanbeige's own benchmark table it beats Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B and Gemma4-31B on most agent tests (for example 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 65.5 on DeepSWE), though Qwen3.8-27B edges it on SWE-Bench Pro and GDPval. Runs with Transformers, SGLang or vLLM (Nanbeige's server examples use four GPUs); community GGUF quants exist for smaller setups. Released Oct 24, 2026; about 500 likes on Hugging Face in its first two days. Pricing: Free open weights (Apache-2.0). Free tier: yes.
- [Hugging Face](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/hugging-face): The hub for open models, datasets and Spaces demos, plus hosted inference. Pricing: PRO from $9/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Claude Code](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/claude-code): Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal, IDE and web. Pricing: Included with paid Claude plans.
- [OpenAI Codex](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/openai-codex): OpenAI's coding agent for the CLI, IDE and cloud tasks. Pricing: Included with ChatGPT plans (limited on Free and Go). Free tier: yes.
- [Warp](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/warp): Agentic terminal and development environment with built-in AI agents. Pricing: Build from $20/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Cline](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/cline): Open-source autonomous coding agent for VS Code. Pricing: Open source.
- [Aider](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/aider): Open-source AI pair programming in your terminal, with git integration. Pricing: Open source.

### Chat Assistants
- [ChatGPT](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/chatgpt): OpenAI's general-purpose AI assistant for chat, writing, code and images. Since Oct 20, 2026 you can lock a chat behind a four-digit PIN or device sign-in so it drops out of your history and search (it is hidden, not end-to-end encrypted). Pricing: Plus $20/mo; lower-cost Go plan also available. Free tier: yes.
- [Claude](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/claude): Anthropic's AI assistant for writing, analysis and coding. New: Claude Duet (research preview, Oct 2026) is a proactive agent app that sends a morning brief from your email and calendar, works on tasks on its own cloud computer and asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything. Waitlist only, for US Pro and Max plans; it uses your plan's usage limits. Plan rename Oct 30, 2026: Max 5x is now Max ($100/mo, 5x Pro's weekly usage) and Max 20x is now Ultra ($200/mo, 10x Pro's weekly usage), with no price change and nothing for existing subscribers to do. Verified Ultra accounts no longer have the rolling five-hour limit, but the weekly limit still applies; Anthropic verifies accounts automatically, and newer accounts keep a temporary limit until then (if you don't see a Current session bar in Settings > Usage, you're verified). Pricing: Pro from $17/mo billed annually ($20 monthly); Max $100/mo; Ultra $200/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Gemini](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/gemini): Google's AI assistant, connected to Google apps and search. For work, the new Gemini agent (Oct 8, 2026) runs inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets and Calendar. New Oct 29, 2026: Gemini can generate, preview and edit files right in the chat (type edits in full screen, or highlight a section and ask for changes). PDFs work on web and mobile; Google Docs, Sheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT and code are web only. Available to all Gemini users. Pricing: Google AI Plus from $4.99/mo (US). Free tier: yes.
- [Grok](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/grok): xAI's AI assistant with real-time knowledge from X and the web. Pricing: Free on the web and in the apps; SuperGrok paid upgrade for higher limits. Free tier: yes.
- [Off Grid AI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/off-grid-ai): Open-source AI assistant that runs entirely on your own phone or computer: chat with local GGUF models, ask about photos, transcribe speech with Whisper, generate images with Stable Diffusion, chat with your documents and call tools or MCP servers, with no account, no API key and no cloud inference. Apps for iPhone, Android and Mac, plus a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux with a local OpenAI-compatible API. Built by Wednesday Solutions; the developer reports 250,000+ downloads, and the mobile repo has about 3,300 GitHub stars (v0.0.118 shipped Oct 23, 2026). Optional paid Pro adds voice replies, on-device memory, phone-to-Mac sync and actions in Gmail, Linear, Jira and Notion that wait for your approval. Pricing: Free and open source (mobile MIT, desktop AGPL-3.0); Pro $119 lifetime or $7.99/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Microsoft Copilot](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/microsoft-copilot): Microsoft's AI companion for chat, search and creation.
- [Le Chat (Mistral)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/le-chat-mistral): Mistral AI's chat assistant, with Mistral Vibe for coding in the CLI, IDE or web. Pricing: Pro from $14.99/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Ollama](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/ollama): Run open models locally with one command, or use Ollama's cloud models when your machine isn't enough. Recursive's new Flint coding model is in the library (ollama run flint:40b), and so is Liquid AI's new LFM3 family of small on-device models. Pricing: Paid plans from $20/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [LM Studio](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/lm-studio): Desktop app (now with the Bionic agent) for downloading and running local LLMs via llama.cpp and MLX. Pricing: Bionic+ from $20/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [DeepSeek](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/deepseek): Chat assistant powered by DeepSeek's open-weight models. DeepSeek has also open-sourced DeepInfer (Apache-2.0), the inference framework behind its own DeepSeek V4.1 Flash service; it targets data-center GPUs (NVIDIA SM100, Huawei Ascend 950), not home PCs.
- [LFM3 (Liquid AI)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/lfm3-liquid-ai): Liquid AI's family of six small open-weight models (about 2B parameters each) for text, vision with video input, audio, combined voice and vision, and fast yes/no style decisions. The text model fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit, has a 256K-token context and is tuned for local agents; every model can be fine-tuned on a single GPU. Runs with llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, MLX and vLLM. Released Oct 27, 2026; benchmark claims are Liquid AI's own. Pricing: Free open weights (LFM Open License 1.0); Liquid API also available. Free tier: yes.

### Image
- [Midjourney](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/midjourney): AI image and video generator known for its distinctive artistic style. Pricing: Basic from $10/mo ($8/mo billed annually).
- [Ideogram](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/ideogram): AI image generator that's strong at rendering text in images. Pricing: Plus from $15/mo billed annually ($20 monthly). Free tier: yes.
- [Leonardo.Ai](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/leonardo-ai): AI image and video generation platform for creators and game assets. Pricing: Essential from $12/mo; free plan has 150 tokens/day. Free tier: yes.
- [Krea](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/krea): Real-time AI image and video generation and enhancement. Pricing: Pro from $21/mo billed yearly ($35 monthly). Free tier: yes.
- [Adobe Firefly](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/adobe-firefly): Adobe's generative AI for images, video and design, built into Creative Cloud.
- [Black Forest Labs (FLUX)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/black-forest-labs-flux): Makers of the FLUX image models, including FLUX 3 Image Klein (Oct 15, 2026): open weights, native 4K, runs on consumer GPUs. New Oct 19: FLUX 3 Max, a video model post-trained by fal with Black Forest Labs, on fal's API for text-, image- and keyframes-to-video (5-20 seconds, 720p or 1080p, audio on by default). fal measured a 10-second clip in about 12 seconds. Launch pricing on fal is 75% off until Nov 7 ($0.0425/s at 720p, $0.0725/s at 1080p), then $0.17/s and $0.29/s. Pricing: API from $0.009/image (FLUX 3 Image Klein at 1K); open weights free for individuals and companies under $5M revenue. Free tier: yes.
- [InvokeAI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/invokeai): Free, open-source AI image studio you run on your own GPU: a unified canvas for inpainting and outpainting, node-based workflows and a gallery, with support for SDXL, SD 3.5, FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen Image and more. About 28,700 GitHub stars; v7.0 is in alpha. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0).
- [Recraft](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/recraft): AI image generator for designers, with vector and brand-style output. Free tier: yes.

### Video
- [Runway](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/runway): AI video generation and editing tools for filmmakers and creators. Pricing: Standard from $12/mo billed annually. Free tier: yes.
- [Synthesia](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/synthesia): Create videos with AI avatars and voiceovers from text. Pricing: Starter from $29/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Pika](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/pika): AI video generator for short creative clips and effects. Pricing: Starter from $10/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Luma AI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/luma-ai): AI video generation with the Dream Machine and Ray models. Pricing: Plus from $30/mo.
- [HeyGen](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/heygen): AI avatar videos, translation and lip-sync. For developers: the HeyGen Voice Turbo Free API model (heygen-voice-1-turbo-free) is free until Nov 30, 2026 with no credit balance needed, for public voices and instant clones (not professional clones). Capacity is shared, so expect occasional 429 errors; HeyGen pitches it for tests and prototypes. Pricing: Creator from $29/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Descript](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/descript): Edit video and podcasts by editing the transcript, with AI tools. Pricing: Hobbyist from $16/mo billed annually ($24 monthly). Free tier: yes.
- [Kling AI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/kling-ai): Kuaishou's AI video generation model and app. Kling 4.0 (fully available Oct 15, 2026) generates up to 30 seconds in one pass with steadier fast motion, and Omni Reference combines up to 15 reference assets and 10 keyframes. It also works through Kling MCP and CLI; 10-bit HDR output and developer API access are coming soon.

### Voice & Audio
- [ElevenLabs](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/elevenlabs): AI voice generation, cloning, dubbing and speech-to-text. New Oct 15: Instant Soundtracks scores an uploaded video with original music and timed sound effects. New Oct 21: Eleven Realtime Translation, live speech-to-speech translation into 90+ languages in a voice you choose, in alpha for ElevenAPI enterprise customers only (contact sales; no public price). New Oct 29: SFX v3, the newest sound effects model, follows prompts that describe several sounds more reliably, handles music and vocals better and cuts harsh artifacts on sounds like gongs and whistles. It's in ElevenCreative (Sound Effects tab, Flows, Studio, Music Editor, mobile app) and ElevenAPI. Pricing: Starter from $6/mo; Creator $22/mo (first month 50% off). Free tier: yes.
- [Suno](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/suno): Generate full songs with vocals from a text prompt. Pricing: Pro from $8/mo billed yearly. Free tier: yes.
- [Udio](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/udio): AI music generation and remixing. Pricing: Standard from $10/mo ($8/mo billed annually). Free tier: yes.
- [Fish Audio](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/fish-audio): AI text-to-speech and voice cloning with a web studio, mobile apps and an API. Its Drama 3 model (Oct 13, 2026) takes plain-language direction (whisper this line, laugh here) and voices multi-character scenes, and the weights are open: free for commercial use under $500K annual revenue (Fish Audio Community License). Its fish-speech repo has about 33,000 GitHub stars. Self-hosting needs a 48GB NVIDIA GPU. Pricing: Plus from $11/mo billed annually ($15 monthly); free plan has 8,000 credits/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Pocket TTS (Kyutai)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/pocket-tts-kyutai): Kyutai's open-source text-to-speech that runs on a plain CPU, no GPU needed, with voice cloning from a short audio clip and streaming output. Version 4.0 (Oct 20, 2026) adds small English models of 18.2M, 6.9M and 1.9M parameters (the 1.9M ones are experimental) plus standalone binaries that don't need Python. About 10,000 GitHub stars. Only clone voices you have permission to use. Pricing: Open source (MIT code; CC-BY-4.0 weights); voice cloning weights need a free Hugging Face terms click-through.
- [Murf AI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/murf-ai): AI voiceover studio and text-to-speech API with 150+ voices in 35+ languages. Pricing: API from $0.01 per 1,000 characters (Falcon); $10 free API credit.

### Agents & Automation
- [n8n](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/n8n): Workflow automation with AI agents; self-hostable and fair-code. Pricing: Cloud Starter from €20/mo billed annually; self-hosted Community Edition free. Free tier: yes.
- [Zapier](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/zapier): Automate work across 7,000+ apps with Zaps and AI agents. Pricing: Professional from $19.99/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [Make](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/make): Visual automation platform with AI agents. Pricing: Free plan with 1,000 credits/mo; paid plans priced by credits. Free tier: yes.
- [Relay.app](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/relay-app): AI workflow automation with human-in-the-loop steps.
- [Muse (Meta)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/muse-meta): Meta's personal AI agent that uses apps for you: email, travel, shopping and more, via app, web or WhatsApp. US-only at launch (Sept 8, 2026). Pricing: Paid plans for heavier use. Free tier: yes.
- [Hermes Agent](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/hermes-agent): Nous Research's open-source personal agent with app connectors, a plugin catalog and one-click local models. Pricing: Open source (MIT).
- [Harness2 (Google Research)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/harness2-google-research): Open-source framework from Google Cloud AI Research that improves an agent's harness (prompts, tools, memory, skills, subagents) instead of its model: it proposes edits, tests them on the same task and keeps what worked for next time. Runs OpenCode or Codex as the executor. About 13,500 GitHub stars two weeks after release; research code, not an official Google product. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0).
- [OpenAI Decisions API](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/openai-decisions-api): OpenAI API for the small, frequent decisions inside apps and agents: classify an input, pick a route or choose the next action. You define a question and the allowed answers, send text, images or JSON, and get back a probability, a choice or a score instead of free text. Built on GPT-6 Luna; OpenAI says it's up to 10x faster than Luna through the Responses API. Generally available Oct 22, 2026, with up to 400 questions per request, prompt caching and GPT-Live integration. Pricing: $0.10 per 1M input tokens ($0.01 cached); no output-token charges.
- [Cloudflare Clairic](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/cloudflare-clairic): Cloudflare's extraction model on Workers AI (@cf/cloudflare/clairic). You send text (plus up to four images) and a list of typed fields, and it returns each value as the type you asked for (text span, number, date, duration, list, estimate or forecast) with a confidence score, or null if it isn't there. It answers in one pass without generating tokens, so it's fast and can't return malformed JSON, though it can still be wrong. Preview since Oct 19, 2026, 65,536-token context; Cloudflare says open weights are coming. Inputs are processed on Cloudflare. Pricing: $0.10 per 1M input tokens; no output-token charges (preview).
- [Lindy](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/lindy): Build AI agents that handle email, meetings and workflows. Pricing: Team from $29.99/mo; $50 in starter credits.

- [GhidraMCP](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/ghidramcp): Open-source MCP server and plugin that lets an AI assistant drive Ghidra, the NSA's free reverse-engineering suite: decompile binaries, list functions, imports and exports, and rename methods and data as it works. About 11,400 GitHub stars; v2.0 shipped Oct 10, 2026 for Ghidra 12.1.4. Analyze malware samples only inside an isolated VM. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); Ghidra is free; model usage billed by your AI provider.

Runs locally in Docker with your own LLM API key, and can scan pull requests in CI. About 71,000 GitHub stars; v1.7.0 shipped Oct 5, 2026. Only test apps you own or have written permission to test. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); Strix Cloud Pro $29/seat/mo, pentests billed separately. Free tier: yes.
- [Shannon (Keygraph)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/shannon-keygraph): Open-source autonomous AI pentester for web apps and APIs from Keygraph. It reads your source code to find likely attack paths, then runs real exploits against the running app and reports only what it could prove ('no exploit, no report'). Runs from the command line with npx and Docker on your own model provider account. About 49,000 GitHub stars; v3.4.0 shipped Oct 6, 2026. Keygraph says never to point it at production or at anything you aren't authorized to test. Pricing: Shannon open source free (AGPL-3.0); Keygraph Pro $50/developer/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [PentAGI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/pentagi): Open-source, self-hosted multi-agent system for autonomous penetration testing from VXControl. Describe a target and goal in plain language and a team of AI agents plans the work, runs 20+ tools such as nmap, Metasploit and sqlmap inside an isolated Docker sandbox, remembers what worked and writes a report, with a web UI plus REST and GraphQL APIs. Works with 10+ cloud model providers or local models through Ollama or vLLM. About 32,000 GitHub stars; v2.2.0 shipped Oct 5, 2026. For authorized testing only. Pricing: Open source (MIT); PentAGI Enterprise available.
- [SkillSpector (NVIDIA)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/skillspector-nvidia): NVIDIA's open-source scanner that checks AI agent skills (for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and MCP) before you install them. It looks for 71 vulnerability patterns across 17 categories, including prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply-chain risk and MCP tool poisoning, then gives a 0-100 risk score with JSON, Markdown or SARIF reports. Fast static checks work offline; an optional LLM pass adds deeper review. Scans Git repos, URLs, zip files or folders, and runs in Docker. About 21,000 GitHub stars; v2.13.1 shipped Oct 23, 2026. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); optional LLM analysis billed by your AI provider.
- [Snyk Agent Scan](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/snyk-agent-scan): Snyk's open-source scanner that finds the AI agents, MCP servers and skills already installed on your machine (Claude Code and Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenCode and more) and checks them for prompt injection, tool poisoning, private-data exposure, destructive capabilities, malicious code and hardcoded secrets. Asks before it starts or contacts each MCP server, and Snyk recommends a sandbox or VM for untrusted configs. Runs with uvx or a signed standalone binary and needs a free Snyk API token; component details are sent to Snyk's Agent Scan API for analysis, with secrets redacted. About 3,200 GitHub stars; v0.6.9 shipped Oct 20, 2026. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); free Snyk account and API token required. Free tier: yes.
- [Cisco Skill Scanner](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/cisco-skill-scanner): Cisco AI Defense's open-source scanner for AI agent skills (Agent Skills format used by Codex and Cursor, plus Claude Code commands with --lenient). It combines YAML and YARA-X rules, code and dataflow analysis and an optional LLM judge that can use cloud or local models, and outputs SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning with a ready-made GitHub Action and a pre-commit hook. Cisco publishes its own measured detection and false-positive rates: rules alone caught 7.7% of malicious test skills at HIGH, and with the LLM judge 66.7% reached MEDIUM or above at a 15.4% false-positive rate, so it says a clean scan is not a guarantee. About 2,600 GitHub stars; 2.3.1 shipped Oct 21, 2026. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); optional LLM judge billed by your AI provider.
- [Strands Box](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/strands-box): Open-source sandbox for AI agents from the Strands Agents project. It runs any agent program inside OS-level isolation and checks its shell commands, Python, network requests and MCP tool calls against default-deny policies (written in the Dogwood policy language), so an agent can only do what a rule permits. Rules can depend on earlier actions, for example blocking an outbound request after the agent read a secrets file. API keys are injected by Box's gateway, so the agent never sees them, and every decision is logged. Written in Rust; preview for Apple silicon Macs only (Linux planned). About 475 GitHub stars; v0.1.0 shipped Oct 7, 2026, with commits daily. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0).
- [1Password for Agents](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/1password-for-agents): 1Password's sign-in layer for personal AI agents, launched Oct 22, 2026. When an agent reaches a login page it asks 1Password for the credential; you see which login it wants and approve or deny on your own device, and 1Password fills the password or one-time code straight into the site, so the agent never sees or stores it. You can disconnect an agent at any time. Integrations for Meta's Muse and Grok Bot are rolling out first; Anthropic's Claude Duet, OpenAI's ChatGPT Work and dots and Town's Townie are listed as coming soon, with Browserbase, Browser Use, Perplexity and others planned. 1Password.com accounts only (not 1Password.eu or .ca), and safeguards vary by integration. Pricing: No extra cost with 1Password Individual and Families plans.
- [CVEngine](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/cvengine): Free, self-hosted external attack-surface scanner with optional AI triage. Add a domain, IP range or URL and it discovers subdomains (bbot), sweeps ports (naabu), fingerprints services (nmap), runs nuclei checks and matches what you run against exploited CVEs from CISA KEV, EPSS, Exploit-DB, Metasploit and other feeds, then confirms what it can with read-only checks that record the exact command they ran. Bring your own AI (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or local Ollama or vLLM) or run it without one; AI-drafted nuclei templates never run until a person approves them. Includes an MCP server and REST API with read-only tokens for agents. One Docker Compose stack on Linux (4GB RAM minimum, 8GB recommended). A fork of reNgine 2.x from a single maintainer, published Oct 24, 2026 and at about 400 GitHub stars two days later. Only scan systems you own or are authorized to test. Pricing: Open source (GPL-3.0).
- [HOL Guard](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/hol-guard): Free, local-first guard for the AI coding agents you already use. It checks shell commands, file access, package installs and MCP tool calls before they run, flags secret exposure, destructive commands, prompt injection and supply-chain risk, and allows, blocks or asks you to approve each action based on your policy. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Cline, OpenCode and others through their hooks, so coverage depends on what each agent exposes. Runs without an account, keeps a local history of every decision, can produce an AI bill of materials and SARIF output for CI, and has an optional Guard Cloud for team policies. Install with pipx (Python 3.10+). About 1,000 GitHub stars and roughly 76,000 PyPI downloads in the past month; v3.58.0 shipped Oct 27, 2026. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); optional Guard Cloud for teams.
- [Zendesk](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/zendesk): Widely used help desk and ticketing platform with an employee service (internal IT and HR) edition. On Oct 26, 2026 Zendesk announced employee service AI agents and advanced action flows that handle onboarding and offboarding, access approvals, laptop lifecycle and badge requests from the help center, Slack or Microsoft Teams, with automations written in plain language. Zendesk says 300 early-access customers ran 6 million workflow executions in five weeks. General availability rolls out Nov 3 to Dec 1, 2026, with 20+ knowledge connectors (Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion and more) and automatic escalation to a ticket. From Nov 3, Growth and Professional plans include 10 automated resolutions per AI agent per month, then $0.99 each. Pricing: Support Team from $19/agent/mo billed annually ($25 monthly); Suite Team $55/agent/mo; 14-day free trial.
- [BotGauge](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/botgauge): Security and reliability testing for AI agents you build. It runs adaptive red-team attacks (prompt injection, policy bypass, tool misuse, multi-turn manipulation), replays each failure with a full trace and turns it into a regression test, then keeps watching the agent in production. Connects through an SDK to OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI and AutoGen. Launched as the #3 product of the day on Product Hunt on Oct 28, 2026.
- [Project Quarry (Cisco)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/project-quarry-cisco): Open-source detection rules for AI agent sessions, from Cisco AI Defense. You write rules that match patterns across messages, tool calls, MCP activity and the order they happen in (for example, a read of a sensitive file followed by an outbound send), and a match returns the evidence with secrets masked. Use it as a runtime guardrail, to review past agent traces or during incident response; it ships a plugin for Codex, Claude Code and MCP hosts plus a starter rule pack. Apache-2.0, released Oct 28, 2026, and still alpha, so the rule syntax may change before v1.0. Pricing: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). Free tier: yes.
- [Mistral Large 4](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/mistral-large-4): Mistral's flagship open-weight model (about 1 trillion parameters total, 49B active per token, 1M-token context, text and image input), released as open weights on Oct 29, 2026 and pitched at coding and defensive cybersecurity: finding, reproducing and patching vulnerabilities, malware analysis and writing detection rules. Mistral reports 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index and a 96.6% average refusal rate on malicious cyber prompts; these are Mistral's own figures. Three reasoning levels (low, medium, high). Far too big for a home PC: self-host on data-center GPUs with vLLM or SGLang, or use it through Mistral Studio, the Mistral API or OpenRouter. Pricing: API $0.70/M input, $2.10/M output tokens; open weights free (Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License; Model-as-a-Service businesses need a commercial license). Free tier: yes.
- [Radar (Skyhook)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/radar-skyhook): Free, open-source Kubernetes UI with a built-in MCP server for AI agents. One binary on your laptop (or a Helm install in-cluster) shows topology, live traffic, an event timeline, Helm and GitOps state, image filesystems and a 44-check cluster audit, with no account. Point Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot or any MCP client at it and the agent gets trimmed, secret-redacted cluster context instead of raw kubectl YAML; diagnosis is read-only by default and write actions follow your Kubernetes RBAC (or run it with --mcp-read-only). About 4,000 GitHub stars; v1.19.0 shipped Oct 29, 2026, the day it made the Product Hunt top 10. Optional Radar Cloud adds alerts and hosted AI investigations. Pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0); Radar Cloud free for up to 3 clusters, Team from $149/cluster/mo. Free tier: yes.
- [REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/rea-reverse-engineer-anything): Free, open-source (MIT) MCP server and CLI that lets your AI coding agent reverse engineer software: native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies and websites, with findings that include the evidence and limits behind each conclusion. Native analysis drives a Ghidra, Hopper, IDA or Kuna install you already have; static JavaScript analysis needs no extra engine, and analysis runs locally. One command (npx rea-agents setup) registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents. The rea-agents npm package was downloaded about 538,000 times in the week of Oct 23-29, 2026 (v6.8.0, Oct 25), and Scientific American profiled it on Oct 30. Only reverse engineer software you own or are allowed to analyze; some users report OpenAI and Anthropic blocking reverse-engineering requests, so check your model provider's terms. Pricing: Free and open source (MIT); you pay for your own agent or model. Free tier: yes.
- [HackAgent](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/hackagent): Open-source (Apache-2.0) red-team toolkit for AI models and agents you own. It runs research-backed jailbreak, prompt-injection and tool-misuse attacks, has judge models score every reply and reports a measured success rate per attack, so you can see whether a fix helped. Use the terminal UI, YAML campaign files you can run in CI, or the hackagent web dashboard. Runs fully local with Ollama and needs no API key; results stay in a local database by default. About 530 GitHub stars; v0.16.0 shipped Oct 20, 2026. For authorized testing only. Pricing: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). Free tier: yes.
- [Elastic Security AI](https://aitrackertool.dev/tools/elastic-security-ai): AI in Elastic Security: automated alert triage and hypothesis-driven threat hunts with ES|QL over your SIEM data.
